title: Minimax Estimation of Causal Expected Shortfall under Arbitrary Record Contamination
banked_reason: Not salvageable within scope — bank downgraded, or re-anchor the proposal (rewind D-1.2).
gap_reasons: The substantive limitation is that the uniform design, exact propensity, and deterministic positive-loss map are supplied, fixing the tail ordering and reducing outcome information to a treated-positive Bernoulli mark.

The prospective consumer does not establish applicability beyond this exact loss geometry, so the narrow statistical scope and undemonstrated practical usefulness constrain the projected paper score and place the contribution below field.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived observable expected-shortfall estimation and matched risk/honest-length orders under known weak-overlap propensity and arbitrary original-record contamination. Math and rubric reviewers passed with no findings; classical source checks were resolved against primary publisher/author excerpts. The result was graded incremental below the field floor because its supplied design and deterministic severity make it a specialized benchmark; an unknown-propensity extension changes the experiment and requires a new proposal, and no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: The normalized clean causal shortfall has minimax squared risk of order \(r_n(\varepsilon,\alpha)^2\), and finite-sample honest connected intervals have minimax expected length of order \(r_n(\varepsilon,\alpha)\), uniformly over the stipulated Lipschitz Bernoulli class, public tail levels, and arbitrary original-record contamination. The explicit bounded estimator extrapolates at unresolved endpoints and otherwise minimizes a fitted positive-tail shortfall objective. The moving-cutoff bound has no growing logarithmic penalty. Legal full-record sampling and contamination pairs match both orders. The consumer is prospective downside evaluation of the fixed all-treatment rule under the criterion of Qi, Pang and Liu.
gap: Fully observed robust ES, binary-IV complier ES asymptotics, positive-overlap potential-outcome CVaR inference, and weak-overlap linear-functional theory leave a distinct joint observation problem: arbitrary original-record corruption and a nonlinear clean tail functional with a moving cutoff.
fill: The focal result couples observable attainment to all-procedure risk and honest-length converses, with the exact submitted \(r_n(\varepsilon,\alpha)\) tested in every allowed regime.
